title: Tenant-aware delta-detection eval harness with local goldens and soft-rollback webhooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Model/config rollouts (kernel selection, quantization profile, routing policy changes) can introduce subtle quality regressions for specific customers, especially on Dedicated and Private deployments where data distributions and prompt templates differ. We need an automated, tenant-scoped regression detector that runs lightweight, privacy-preserving evals against a customer-local golden set and triggers operator/webhook workflows to rollback or quarantine a rollout.

Scope: Build a tenant-local delta detection harness that: (1) orchestrates small periodic eval runs when model or config changes are deployed to a tenant; (2) stores encrypted golden references per-tenant (customer-managed KMS optional) and runs diffs locally for Private/Dedicated; (3) computes a compact delta score and classification (regression/no-regression/uncertain) using configurable thresholds; (4) exposes result events via webhook + Console alarm and can open automated rollback/canary gates.

Non-goals: Full-scale long-running eval pipelines, replacing existing cross-tenant eval suites, or storing raw customer prompt/response payloads in hosted telemetry logs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: The eval harness runs for a tenant when a model or applicable config variant (quantization, batch policy) is deployed and completes within the configured SLA (default < 5 minutes for a quick-check run).
A2: Goldenset is stored in an encrypted blob with tenant-scoped access controls; Private/Dedicated installs can opt for customer KMS.
A3: Delta score calculation published (delta_metric, threshold) and documented; Console shows per-tenant pass/fail/uncertain and tokenized breakdown for first-level triage.
A4: Webhook event with structured payload (tenant, delta_score, top-regressions) delivered on completion and on threshold-cross; webhook can be configured per-project in Console.
A5: Soft-rollback automation exists: a canary-stage block that prevents full rollout when delta_score > critical threshold and creates a PM/Eng incident card.
A6: For Private installs, no plaintext customer prompts or responses are sent to Redwood hosted telemetry; only encrypted hashes and aggregate metrics are transmitted (customer opt-in documented).
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Security, and Console teams. Agreed on two run modes: quick-check (fast, small sample) and extended (larger sample for root cause).
2026-03-11: Prototype spec for delta metric drafted (weighted median of per-prompt semantic similarity + token-level quality regression signals). Shared to #evals-channel for feedback.
2026-03-12: Security review sync: requirement for customer-managed KMS for Private installs and strict telemetry gating accepted; added opt-in flag for hosted customers.

2026-03-13: Engineering spike completed (ENG-5123): local runner can execute 50 sample prompts against pinned model and return a delta score; storing goldenset encrypted using mock KMS. Small perf regression observed on 2x quantized models — investigated.
2026-03-14: Console hooks spec completed; placeholder webhook payload and retry semantics documented. Opening ENG follow-up tasks for rollback automation and webhook retries.
decisions: D1: Use a compact delta score exposed as a single float and a categorical label (pass/uncertain/fail) for automation gates.
D2: Goldensets are tenant-owned assets: stored encrypted, accessible only by tenant-scoped runner; hosted customers can opt-in to share encrypted hashes for cross-tenant benchmarking.
D3: Default quick-check sample size is 50 prompts; teams can configure extended runs (200 prompts) for higher confidence during major upgrades.

D4: For Private/Dedicated, runner executes inside customer network when possible; only aggregated metrics (delta_score, counts) leave the tenant environment unless customer opts into richer telemetry.
risks: R1: False positives could block safe rollouts if thresholds not tuned — mitigation: make rollback soft by default and require human confirmation for critical customers.
R2: Customer privacy concerns around storing golden prompts; mitigation: tenant-owned encrypted goldens, optional KMS, and default to sending only hashed aggregates to hosted telemetry.
R3: Performance overhead on Dedicated nodes during eval runs — mitigation: schedule quick-checks during low-util windows and cap concurrency per-tenant.
notes: Follow-up: run a pilot with two Dedicated customers in April; collect false-positive rate and time-to-decision metrics.
Action: schedule a privacy AMA with Legal to finalize consent language for hosted customers sharing aggregated hashes.
Consideration: tie delta detector to Optimize suggestions so that when a regression is benign and expected (e.g., token-economy tradeoff), teams can accept with annotated rationale.
